title: Weddings, festivals & occasions
goal: Invite and be invited, wish people well at festivals, weddings and birthdays, give blessings, and know what to say and do at Maharashtra's big celebrations.
intro:
Maharashtra's year is a string of celebrations: **गुढीपाडवा** (the Marathi New Year), ten loud days of **गणेशोत्सव**, **दसरा**, **दिवाळी** with its tins of **फराळ**, **संक्रांत** with **तिळगूळ** — and in between, weddings with their **हळद**, **अक्षता** and endless lunches.

This unit gives you the greetings for each one, the vocabulary of a Marathi wedding, and two pieces of grammar that every occasion needs: the **optative** for wishes and blessings (**तुला यश मिळो** 'may you succeed', **सगळ्या इच्छा पूर्ण होवोत** 'may all your wishes come true'), and the many ways Marathi hosts say 'be sure to come': **नक्की या**, **आवर्जून या**, **यायचंच हं!**

grammar.title: Wishes and blessings: मिळो, होवो and -च्या शुभेच्छा
grammar.body:
Marathi has a special verb form for wishing something on someone — the **optative**, 'may it…'. You have already met one: त्यांच्या आत्म्याला शांती **लाभो** (Unit 30).

**How to build it:** stem + **ओ** when the thing wished is singular, + **ओत** when it is plural. Consonant stems just add it: मिळ → **मिळो**, लाभ → **लाभो**, कर → **करो**, ठेव → **ठेवो**. Vowel stems add **व** first: हो → **होवो / होवोत**, ये → **येवो**, जा → **जावो**.

**Who is the subject?** The thing you wish for. The lucky person takes **-ला**: तुला यश **मिळो** 'may you succeed' (lit. may success come to you), नवीन वर्ष तुम्हाला आनंदाचं **जावो** 'may the new year go happily for you'. When God or Bappa does the blessing, they are the subject: देव तुमचं भलं **करो** 'God bless you', बाप्पा सगळ्यांना सुखी **ठेवो**.

**Elders' blessings** often use the plain command instead: **सुखी राहा** 'be happy', **मोठा हो** 'grow up big' (to a child), **यशस्वी हो** 'be successful'. When you touch an elder's feet (पाया पडणे) this is what you will hear back.

**Everyday greetings** use **-च्या शुभेच्छा** for an occasion: वाढदिवसा**च्या** शुभेच्छा, लग्ना**च्या** शुभेच्छा, दसऱ्या**च्या** शुभेच्छा; and **-साठी** for something ahead of someone: नवीन नोकरी**साठी** शुभेच्छा 'all the best for the new job'. Add **हार्दिक** 'heartfelt' or **खूप खूप** for warmth.

**The trap:** the optative agrees with what is wished, not with the person: तुझी स्वप्नं (pl) पूर्ण **होवोत**, but तुझं स्वप्न (sg) पूर्ण **होवो**.

examples.native: तुला नवीन नोकरीत खूप यश मिळो.
examples.roman: tulā navīn nokrīt khūp yash miḷo.
examples.en: May you do really well in your new job.
May your married life be a happy one.
May the new year be a happy one for you.
All the best for the new job!

grammar.title: 'Be sure to…': नक्की, आवर्जून, यायचंच, विसरू नकोस
grammar.body:
Marathi invitations push warmly, and a single 'do come' can sound half-hearted. Hosts stack up these ways of saying 'be sure to':

- **नक्की** 'definitely' + command: नक्की **या** (तुम्ही), नक्की **ये** (तू).
- **आवर्जून** 'making a special point of it': आवर्जून या — the warmest invitation word. Wedding cards say **आपण आवर्जून उपस्थित राहावे** 'please be sure to attend' (the written -आवे of Unit 31).
- **stem + आयचं + च** 'you simply have to': the 'supposed to' form of Unit 15 plus the emphatic **च**: लग्नाला **यायचंच** हं! 'you absolutely have to come to the wedding!'. With an object it agrees: मोदक (pl) **खायचेच**, मिठाई (f) **खायचीच**. **हं** at the end is a friendly 'OK?'.
- **stem + आयला विसरू नकोस / नका** 'don't forget to': फोटो **काढायला विसरू नकोस**, आहेर **आणायला विसरू नका**.
- Negative instructions use **-आयचं नाही**: उशीर करायचा नाही 'don't be late'.

**Answering:** **नक्की येणार!** 'I'll definitely be there', **हो, येतो / येते** 'yes, I'll come'. **प्रयत्न करतो** 'I'll try' is the polite way of saying probably not — and everyone knows it.

**The trap:** -आयचंच is not a past tense. यायचंच means 'have to come', not 'came'.

examples.en: Do make a point of coming for our Ganpati.
You absolutely have to come to the engagement!
Don't forget to bring the gift.
You simply have to try Mum's modaks!
I'll definitely be there, don't worry!

dialogue.title: Two invitations
dialogue.setting: Aditi catches her friend Kabir after college in Pune, a week before Ganeshotsav.

lines.speaker: Aditi
lines.en: Kabir, what are you doing this Saturday?

lines.en: We have Ganpati at home. Do come for the evening aarti.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.en: I'll definitely come! There'll be modaks, right?

lines.speaker: Aditi

lines.en: Of course — Mum's steamed modaks! You have to try them.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.native: मग तर नक्की. काय आणू? फुलं, मिठाई?
lines.roman: mag tar nakkī. kāy āṇū? phulaṃ, miṭhāī?
lines.en: Then I'm definitely coming. What shall I bring? Flowers, sweets?

lines.speaker: Aditi
lines.native: काही नको, फक्त वेळेवर ये. आणि हो, पुढच्या महिन्यात माझ्या ताईचं लग्न आहे.
lines.roman: kāhī nako, phakta veḷevar ye. āṇi ho, puḍhchyā mahinyāt mājhyā tāītsaṃ lagna āhe.
lines.en: Nothing, just come on time. Oh, and my sister's getting married next month.

lines.speaker: Kabir
lines.en: Oh wow! Congratulations! Where is it?

lines.speaker: Aditi

lines.roman: nāshiklā. hī ghe patrikā. muhūrta sakāḷī akrā vādzūn bāvīs miniṭānnī āhe.

lines.speaker: Aditi

lines.roman: ho, muhūrta tsukvāytsā nāhī! āṇi akṣatā ṭākāylā visarū nakos.
lines.en: Yes, you can't miss the muhurat! And don't forget to throw the akshata.

lines.speaker: Kabir

lines.roman: ṭhīk āhe. āṇi āher kāy karāytsā?
lines.en: OK. And what should I give as a gift?

lines.speaker: Aditi
lines.en: You being there is the gift!

culture:
**Ganeshotsav** (August–September) is Maharashtra's biggest festival. Lokmanya Tilak turned it into a public festival in Pune in 1893, and today every neighbourhood **मंडळ** sets up a pandal while many families keep a Ganpati at home for one and a half, five, seven or ten days. Friends and neighbours are invited for the evening **आरती** and **मोदक**. On the last day the idols are carried to the river or sea in processions with **ढोल-ताशा** troupes, and the crowd shouts **गणपती बाप्पा मोरया, पुढच्या वर्षी लवकर या!** 'come back soon next year!'.

At **Diwali** families make tins of **फराळ** (chakli, karanji, ladoo, shankarpali) and exchange them with neighbours, hang an **आकाशकंदील**, draw **रांगोळी** at the door, and sisters wave a lamp around their brothers at **भाऊबीज**. At **Sankranti** people give **तिळगूळ** with the line **तिळगूळ घ्या, गोड गोड बोला** — forgive old quarrels and speak sweetly. **Gudi Padwa**, the Marathi New Year, is marked by a **गुढी** raised outside the house and processions in traditional dress.

A Marathi wedding starts at a precise **मुहूर्त**. The priest and guests sing the **मंगलाष्टकं** while a cloth is held between bride and groom; at the final **शुभमंगल सावधान** it drops and everyone throws **अक्षता**. Many invitations say **कृपया आहेर आणू नये** 'please, no gifts' — take your blessings and turn up for the meal. At birthdays the mother often does **औक्षण** (waving a lamp, **ओवाळणे**) before the cake is cut.

tip.title: Festival greetings
tip.body:
- Any occasion: **…च्या (हार्दिक) शुभेच्छा!** — दसऱ्याच्या शुभेच्छा, गुढीपाडव्याच्या शुभेच्छा.
- Ganpati: **गणपती बाप्पा मोरया!** — answered **मंगलमूर्ती मोरया!**
- Sankranti: hand over sesame sweets with **तिळगूळ घ्या, गोड गोड बोला**.
- 'At' a festival is **-ला**: दिवाळीला, गणपतीला, संक्रांतीला.

sentences.native: गणपती बाप्पा मोरया! पुढच्या वर्षी लवकर या!
sentences.roman: gaṇpatī bāppā moryā! puḍhchyā varṣī lavkar yā!
sentences.en: Hail Lord Ganesh! Come back soon next year!
We have Ganpati at home for ten days.
Mum makes modaks for Ganpati.
The dhol-tasha was playing in the procession.
At Sankranti people give everyone tilgul.
The new year begins at Gudi Padwa.
There's always something sweet at home for a festival.
Happy Dussehra!
The drums went on all night.

sentences.native: हा घे तिळगूळ, आता गोड बोल!
sentences.roman: hā ghe tiḷgūḷ, ātā goḍ bol!
sentences.en: Here, have some tilgul — now say only sweet things!

tip.title: Be sure to: नक्की, आवर्जून, यायचंच
tip.body:
- **नक्की** / **आवर्जून** + polite command: नक्की **या**, आवर्जून **या** 'do be sure to come'.
- 'You simply must': stem + **आयचं + च**: लग्नाला **यायचंच** हं!
- 'Don't forget to': stem + **आयला विसरू नकोस / नका**.
- Reply **नक्की येणार!** — **प्रयत्न करतो** often means no.
tip.pattern: आवर्जून या · यायचंच · आणायला विसरू नका

sentences.en: Do make a point of coming to my brother's wedding.

sentences.native: तू यायचंच हं, नाहीतर मी बोलणार नाही!
sentences.roman: tū yāytsaṃts haṃ, nāhītar mī bolṇār nāhī!
sentences.en: You absolutely have to come, or I'm not speaking to you!

tip.title: May it…: मिळो, होवो
tip.body:
- Wish something on someone with stem + **ओ** (plural **ओत**): **मिळो**, **करो**, **ठेवो**; vowel stems add व: **होवो**, **येवो**, **जावो**.
- What's wished is the subject; the person takes -ला: तुला यश **मिळो**.
- It agrees with what's wished: स्वप्नं (pl) पूर्ण **होवोत**.
- Elders also bless with the command: **सुखी राहा**.

sentences.en: May you be very successful.
May all your wishes come true.
May the new house bring you luck.
May Bappa keep you happy.
Grandma gave them both her blessings.
May your business prosper.
Have a great year. (lit. may this year go well for you)
Touch your elders' feet and take their blessings.
May you both be happy all your lives.
